ra: Eponymous founder of the Kubrawiyya.
Kubrawi master in the line of Najm al-Din Kubra.
Established the Chishtiyya in India as its founding master.
Chishti saint of Delhi.
Punjabi Chishti saint.
Pre-eminent Chishti saint of Delhi.
Lay disciple within the Chishti circle of Nizam al-Din.
Eponymous founder of the Naqshbandiyya.
Leading Naqshbandi master of the Timurid era.
Naqshbandi poet and hagiographer.
Founder-patron of the Bektashiyya.
Founder of the Ni'matullahi order.
Eponymous founder of the Badawiyya.
Stepson and chief disciple of Ibn al-Arabi.
Systematized Ibn al-Arabi's doctrine of wahdat al-wujud.
Drew his Lama'at from Qunawi's expositions of Ibn al-Arabi.
His Lama'at versifies Ibn al-Arabi's metaphysics of love.
Gulshan-i Raz is a verse summary of Ibn al-Arabi's wahdat al-wujud.
Al-Insan al-Kamil develops Ibn al-Arabi's Perfect Man.
Composed commentary on and verse in the wahdat al-wujud tradition.
Contemporary of Ibn al-Arabi's circle sharing the contemplation of divine beauty in form.
Foremost disciple and successor of Mu'in al-Din Chishti.
Successor of Bakhtiar Kaki in the Delhi Chishti line.
Khalifa and chief successor of Baba Farid.
Devoted disciple of Nizam al-Din Awliya.
Carried forward the Naqshbandi path of Baha al-Din.
Affiliated to the Naqshbandiyya through Khwaja Ahrar.
Of the Firdausiyya, a Suhrawardi branch in India.
His Safaviyya silsila descends through the broader Suhrawardi-Zahidi line.
Transmitted the Kubrawi visionary path founded by Najm al-Din Kubra.
Turkish saint-poet writing in the wake of Rumi's Anatolian devotional milieu.
Persian mystical poetry sharing Rumi's idiom of divine love and longing.
Kashmiri tradition links Nund Rishi's path to the example of Lal Ded.
Kashmiri contemporary devotion overlapping with the Hamadani Sufi presence.
Counted among the great popular saints venerated alongside Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani.
Counted among the four great qutbs of Egyptian Sufism with al-Badawi.
Heir to the sober contemplative tradition consolidated by al-Ghazali.
Some silsilas link Mu'in al-Din's early training to the Central Asian milieu of Kubra's contemporaries.
